html:
SMTO-CTR-0015 — A check found a password or secret written into the task plan

GUID: 10398579-a3ff-4e24-917d-a5fdeb1e28f9
Slug: task-contract-secret-value
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the plan SMTO writes from a request) found a password or other secret written out in the plan's text, where others could read it. The check didn't run or change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Remove the password, key or token from your request text. Don't paste it into the message again. Anything written in the request can end up in the plan, which is shown and saved as normal text.
  2. Save the secret as a parameter in the Parameter Store, then refer to it in your message by typing @ and choosing it. A saved parameter lets SMTO use the value without writing it into the plan.
  3. Send the corrected request as a new message so SMTO writes a new plan. Once the secret is out of the request, it's safe to try again, and the new plan is checked from scratch.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, and the plan shows only the @ reference, not the secret itself.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details, check that the copied text doesn't contain the secret, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. If others may have seen the secret, ask whoever owns it to change it. Don't resend the same request with the secret in it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Offline validate_contract found a supplied known secret value verbatim in the rendered contract data (outside the coverage field).

What this means

  • Offline contract inspection finds a supplied known secret literal in rendered contract data outside its coverage field. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Offline contract inspection finds a supplied known secret literal in rendered contract data outside its coverage field.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the protected-material match without echoing it into public diagnostics or assuming every secret can be detected.

How to fix it

  • validate_contract in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_models.py raised secret_value because one of the supplied secrets appears in the canonical contract excluding coverage. Remove the literal from the source and contract, store the value in the Parameter Store and reference it with an @parameter mention (or another supported private credential reference), then regenerate; do not echo the matched value into diagnostics, and note that an undetected secret is not proof of absence.
  • Remove the detected literal from public contract content and use the supported private credential/reference flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected contract uses the supported private reference and contains no detected protected literal.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
